notes: The record of the comparison SLOPE-RASTER already sits at E4 on. It is written after the fact, from artifacts that were committed at the time; what it adds is that the evidence is now a citable record with a frozen protocol behind it instead of prose in a register.

No candidate-output artifact is listed because none is committed. The candidate side is recomputed from input-dem.asc by tests/slopeCrossCheck.test.ts on every run, which is stronger than a stored copy: a stored copy can drift from the code it claims to come from, and this cannot.

The reference was re-run on 2026-07-30 from the command in command.txt, with GDAL 3.13.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gdal, and reproduced slope-gdal.asc byte for byte (sha256 982c8bf3656ff8db48c154eb7116ca8eafd190ee500bdefddb98c811e8135557). The original run recorded its version, platform and command but not its executable path; the path below is the one that reproduced the artifact, not a guess at the original.

This is two implementations of one algorithm on one analytic surface. It catches coding errors. It does not validate the choice of Horn, it says nothing about the point-cloud-to-DTM path because it starts from a DEM, and it is not accuracy against ground truth.

reference.containerPinningNote: A container digest is the pin this record wants. No container runtime was used for these references, so no image digest exists to record; the executable path, the version GDAL reports, the exact command line and the artifact's own sha256 stand in for it. The reproduction on 2026-07-30 is what makes that substitution checkable rather than asserted.
reference.commandLine: gdal raster slope input-dem.asc slope-gdal.asc --gradient-alg Horn --unit degree --xscale 1 --yscale 1 --no-edges --of AAIGrid

datasets.description: The frozen analytic DEM: z = a.x^2 + b.y^2 + c.x.y + d.x + e.y, 120 x 100 cells at 1 m, slope about 0.05 to 16.4 degrees. The cross and linear terms are what make a north-south flip or an east-west mirror visible.
GDAL 3.13.1 Horn slope in degrees on that DEM, the reference side of the comparison.

parameterSets.description: Horn gradient, degrees, projected metre grid, one-cell border excluded on both sides.

statusReason: All 11,564 interior cells are within the preregistered 0.5 degree tolerance, with a maximum difference of 0.0000368 degree; GDAL against the closed-form gradient agrees on the same cells, so the reference is the raster the command says it is.

unsupported: The one-cell border. The comparison drops it because the reference command leaves it undefined, and the border is where this project's kernel and gdaldem -compute_edges are known to differ: the matrix under validation/cross-implementation/raster-matrix/ measured a shortfall of up to 16.2 degrees there.
Slopes above about 16.4 degrees, which is the steepest this surface reaches.
Geographic grids. This DEM declares no CRS and its axes are metres; the anisotropic per-axis cell-metre path is not exercised here.
Any vertical unit other than metre. A foot-vertical grid is a different parameter set and has not been run.
The point-cloud-to-DTM pipeline. This study starts from a DEM and says nothing about how one is produced.
Accuracy. Agreement with GDAL is agreement between two implementations of Horn's method, not a measurement against ground truth.
